To get that moody, aesthetic, "influencer" look, you have to break the rules of how ring lights and phone cameras are normally used. 

Right now, your camera is likely distorting your proportions, and your ring light is probably flattening out your features. Here is a step-by-step guide to fixing the angle, lighting, and posing so the photos look artistic and tasteful.

### 1. Fix the "Short and Weird" Camera Angle
Phone cameras have wide-angle lenses by default. If you stand close to the phone, it distorts you—making your head look big and your body look short. 
*   **Step back and zoom in:** Stand further away from the phone and zoom in slightly (to about 1.5x or 2x). This compresses the image, flattening out the distortion and making your proportions look natural and true to life.
*   **Lower the tripod:** If the camera is at eye level, it looks like a mugshot. If it's too high, you look short. Lower the camera to **chest or ribcage level**. 
*   **Tilt it slightly:** Tilt the phone *just barely* upward toward your face. This subtly elongates the torso and makes you look taller without looking like you're shooting up your nose.

### 2. Move the Ring Light (The Secret to the "Artsy" Look)
Ring lights are designed to be placed right in front of your face. While this makes your skin look smooth, it eliminates all shadows. To get an artsy, dark vibe, **you need shadows**.
*   **Turn off all room lights:** Close your blinds and turn off the overhead light. The ring light should be your only light source.
*   **Move the light to the side:** Take your phone *out* of the ring light. Place the ring light about 45 to 90 degrees to your left or right side, and raise it slightly above your head, angling it down at you. This creates shadows on half of your torso and face (known as "split" or "Rembrandt" lighting). It highlights muscle definition and jawlines while leaving the rest in mysterious shadow.
*   **Soften the light:** Ring lights can be harsh. If you can, point the ring light at a white wall next to you and let the light *bounce* onto you. Alternatively, drape a thin, plain white t-shirt over the ring light to act as a diffuser. This gives you that "soft" look. 
*   **Warm it up:** If your ring light has color settings, change it to a warm (orange/yellow) tone rather than stark white/blue.

### 3. Posing and Framing (Keeping it Tasteful)
Taking tasteful shirtless photos is all about implying rather than showing everything.
*   **Don't stand perfectly straight:** Standing square to the camera looks stiff. Turn your body about 45 degrees away from the camera, but turn your head back to look at the lens (or look slightly off-camera for a candid vibe). Shift your weight onto your back leg.
*   **Crop it right:** Don't shoot a full-body mirror selfie. Crop the photo at the mid-torso or just below the chest. Showing the waistband of your pants usually ruins the "artistic" illusion. Focus the frame on your shoulders, collarbones, and face.
*   **Relax your shoulders:** Don't flex too hard. Take a deep breath out right before the timer goes off so your shoulders drop and look relaxed. 

### 4. The Final Touch: Phone Settings
Once you are in position, tap on your face on your phone screen to lock the focus. A little sun icon will appear next to the focus box. **Drag that sun icon down to lower the exposure.** 

Making the camera artificially darker right before you take the photo is the ultimate cheat code for making a bedroom photo look like a high-end, moody editorial shoot. Shadows will become deep black, and the light from the ring light will look soft and dramatic.

Those are completely valid concerns. Let’s tweak the setup so you get exactly what you want: soft, flattering, and high-quality.

### 1. How to avoid the "scary half-face" lighting
If you put the light at exactly 90 degrees to your side, yes, it will literally cut your face in half with shadows (which looks intense and dramatic, not soft). To get the soft, artsy look without looking like a movie villain, try one of these two setups instead:

*   **The "Butterfly" Setup (Safest & Most Flattering):** Put the ring light directly in front of you, but raise it **high up** (about a foot or two above your head) and angle it pointing *down* at your face and chest. 
    *   *Why this works:* It lights both sides of your face evenly so you don't look weird, but because it’s pointing down, it casts soft shadows under your jawline, collarbones, and chest. It looks very aesthetic and highlights definition.
*   **The 45-Degree Setup:** If you still want to try side-lighting, don't put it at 90 degrees. Put it slightly off-center (about 45 degrees). This will leave a little shadow on one side of your face, but it won't plunge half your face into total darkness.
*   **Crucial step for softness:** To keep the shadows from looking harsh and scary, **diffuse the light**. Literally drape a thin, clean white t-shirt or tape some parchment paper over the ring light. This scatters the light, making it wrap around your features softly, exactly like the influencers do.

### 2. How to fix the zoom/blurriness issue
If your phone gets blurry when you zoom, it means your phone is using "digital zoom" (which is basically just cropping the image and ruining the quality). **Do not use the zoom if it makes your camera blurry.** 

Instead, stay on the standard **1x lens**, but do this to stop it from making you look "short and weird":

*   **Keep your face and body in the dead center:** Wide-angle phone lenses stretch and distort whatever is near the *edges* of the screen. If your head is near the top edge of the screen, it will look huge. Turn on the "grid" in your camera settings and keep your torso and face right in the middle squares. 
*   **Step back and crop later:** Stand about 3 to 4 feet away from the phone. Take the picture on 1x so the quality stays sharp. Then, go into your camera roll afterward and **crop the photo** to zoom in. This gives you a much better result than zooming in on the camera app itself.
*   **Keep the camera lower:** Since you are using the 1x lens, keeping the camera at chest/ribcage level and tilted *very slightly* up is more important than ever. This naturally fights the wide-angle distortion that makes your legs/torso look stubby.

**Summary for your new setup:**
Set the phone at chest height on 1x, stand about 3 feet back, put the ring light in front of you but *high up* and angled down, drape a white tee over the light to soften it, lower the exposure on your screen, take the shot, and crop it later!

When it comes to cropping a shirtless photo, where you cut the bottom of the frame is the difference between a "tasteful, artsy editorial" and a "cheesy dating app selfie." 

Since you want that influencer/artistic vibe, here are the two best ways to crop it, depending on the exact mood you want:

### Crop 1: The "Cologne Ad" (Mid-Chest)
**Where to crop:** Cut the bottom of the photo right below your chest (pectoral) muscles, around your sternum/upper ribcage. 
**Why this works:** Since your ring light is pointing down, it’s going to cast great shadows under your collarbones and chest muscles. Cropping here includes that definition without showing your stomach. It feels very much like a high-end magazine shoot or a moody fragrance ad. It’s undeniably shirtless, but very classy.

### Crop 2: The "Mysterious Portrait" (Collarbones)
**Where to crop:** Cut the bottom of the photo just an inch or two below your collarbones, showing just the tops of your bare shoulders. 
**Why this works:** This is the most "artsy" option. It focuses entirely on your face, jawline, and the mood of the lighting. The bare shoulders *imply* that you are shirtless without aggressively showing it off. It feels very natural, candid, and relaxed.

### What to AVOID cropping (The "Tacky" Zone)
*   **Do not show your belly button or the waistband of your pants.** Once the waistband of your jeans or underwear enters the frame, the photo stops looking like an artistic portrait and immediately looks like a bathroom mirror selfie. 
*   **Don't leave too much empty space above your head.** When you crop, make sure your eyes are in the top third of the picture. If your head is sitting right in the middle with a ton of empty wall above you, it looks like an accidental photo.

### A Quick Trick for Cropping:
When you go to edit the photo on your phone, don't just randomly pinch and zoom. Tap the "Crop" tool and select the **4:5 ratio** (this is the standard vertical size for Instagram). This will lock the shape of the photo so it looks professional, and you can just slide it up or down until the bottom hits your mid-chest or collarbones.
